title: A work package's gate passes unjudged when its criteria use a one-digit group (AC-1.1)
body:
A work package's gate passes without judging any of its criteria when they are written with a one-digit group, eg `AC-1.1`, a form hv ruled conforming. Read on 2026-11-19 (vc, confirming the Highlander sweep banked at `refs/bank/vc/st0095/highlander-A-intentsvcs-20261119`); not driven through the binary.

- The gate asks for its package's group as `format!("{seq:02}")`, so `01` for WP-01 (`contract.rs:28-33`).
- `contract::group_of` returns the text between the dash and the dot, so `1` for `AC-1.1` (`contract.rs:60-65`), and the gate compares the two as strings (`contract.rs:880-884`).
- So no criterion is in scope, and the gate passes by its roll-up to the thread's contract (`contract.rs:888-896`). `wp done` then closes the package with its criteria unjudged; only the thread's own close judges them.
- `views::group_heading` (`views.rs:1301-1318`) and doctor's `group_seq` (`doctor.rs:1427-1431`) parse the group as a number, so `acceptance.md` shows those criteria under WP-01 while its gate does not count them.
- `preconditions.rs:437-443` counts 182 one-digit rows across three estates.

Expected: one parse of a criterion's group, owned with the other id concerns by `intentsvcs::id`, so `1` and `01` name the same ordinal package everywhere. ST0095's WP-09 (cc) takes it, with a test that a package whose criteria use a one-digit group is blocked by them.
